samples.summary: No upper bound on `dp` anywhere; an out-of-range decimal count makes `safeFormat` throw an uncaught `RangeError`, and the value is persisted to the shared document (render DoS reachable from an untrusted .xlsx)
samples.evidence:
`safeFormat` (format.ts:9-19) only guards against a bad *locale*: the `catch` re-invokes `value.toLocaleString('en-US', options)` with the SAME `options`, so an out-of-range `minimumFractionDigits`/`maximumFractionDigits` (valid range 0–100, 0–20 on older engines) throws a second, uncaught `RangeError` out of `formatValue`. `formatValue` is called on every display path (`Sheet.toDisplayString`, sheet.ts:967; the render helper at sheet.ts:4719) and neither is wrapped in a try/catch (only three `catch` sites exist in view/worksheet.ts, none around render), so the grid stops rendering.

Nothing clamps `dp` on the way in:
- Untrusted file input: `mapNumberFormat` derives `dp` straight from the attacker-supplied xlsx `formatCode` via `decimalPlaces` — `code.match(/\.(0+)/)` then `match[1].length` (packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-styles.ts:178-181, used at :279, :282, :297) with no cap. A workbook containing `<numFmt formatCode="0.` + 200 zeros + `"/>` yields `{nf:'number', dp:200}`, which is written into the collaborative document and then crashes the render for the importer and every collaborator who opens the sheet — a persisted, remote-file-triggered availability failure.
- The code under review is the new owner of the step and clamps only the low side: `const clamped = stepped < 0; const target = clamped ? 0 : stepped;` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4208-4209) — `changeDecimals(1)` increments without limit, so ~101 Increase clicks reach the same crash. The new pre-write check also evaluates `formatValue(value, nf, target, options)` (sheet.ts:4295) with that unbounded `target`, so the throw can now happen inside `changeDecimals` itself, before/instead of any write.
Fix directions: clamp `dp` where it is parsed and written (importer + `changeDecimals`), and/or make `safeFormat` fall back to an options-sanitised call rather than re-throwing.
searchedFor: Grep `dp:|\.dp\b|Math\.min\(.*dp|clamp` across packages/sheets/src (no upper-bound clamp on dp anywhere)
Grep `function decimalPlaces` in packages/sheets/src/import (unbounded zero count from formatCode)
Grep `catch` in packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts (no try/catch around the render path)

samples.summary: New public model mutators (`changeDecimals`, `unsetRangeStyleValues`) carry no read-only/permission check; the only gate is in the view layer, so the model is one careless call site away from a read-only bypass
samples.evidence: The read-only gate for this feature is `if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return;` in the view (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:535 and :545). The logic it protected now lives in `Sheet.changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4195) and the new public `Sheet.unsetRangeStyleValues` (sheet.ts:4332), which write to the store (`setSheetStyle`/`setColumnStyle`/`setRowStyle`/`setRangeStyles`/`set`/`delete`, sheet.ts:4440-4497) with no permission check of their own. I enumerated the call sites: `Grep '\.sheet\??\.(setRangeStyle|setStyle|changeDecimals|unsetRangeStyleValues)'` returns only spreadsheet.ts:223, :536, :546, and `sheet` is `private` on `Spreadsheet` (spreadsheet.ts:63) while `Worksheet`'s handlers all short-circuit on `this.readOnly`, so there is no bypass today — hence minor, defense-in-depth only. Note the enforcement is client-side either way; a viewer with a write-capable document token is not stopped by these checks, which is pre-existing and out of this diff's scope. Adding a mutation guard at the model layer (or routing all style mutations through one gated entry point) would keep the newly widened public surface from becoming a bypass later.
searchedFor: Grep `_readOnly|readOnly` across packages/sheets/src (gates live in view/spreadsheet.ts and view/worksheet.ts only)
Grep `(?i)protect|locked|permission|canEdit|isEditable` in packages/sheets/src (no protected-range/permission concept in the sheets model)
Read packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts (ReadOnlyStore is for query results, not a permission layer)

verdict.reason: Verified independently: safeFormat's catch re-invokes toLocaleString with the SAME options object (format.ts:14-18), so an out-of-range fraction-digit count throws an uncaught RangeError out of formatValue (decimals flows unbounded from dp at format.ts:119 into minimum/maximumFractionDigits at :127-130, :141-146, :151-155). I searched wide for the missing clamp and found none: normalizeStylePatch/mergeStylePatch (range-styles.ts:14-57), the shared write-path normalizer used by setRangeStyle (sheet.ts:1807-1810, 1844, 1949, 3673), only strip undefined keys; types.ts:101 types dp as a bare number; repo-wide grep for MAX_DECIMAL/MAX_DP/maximumFractionDigits turns up no cap; the importer writes decimalPlaces() output verbatim (xlsx-styles.ts:178-181 -> :297 -> :413 -> xlsx-importer.ts:349). A custom numFmtId>=164 with formatCode "0." + 200 zeros falls through every branch of mapNumberFormat to :296-297 yielding {nf:'number', dp:200}. The render path is also unguarded: formatValue is called per-cell at gridcanvas.ts:1596 and :1777, gridcanvas.ts contains zero try/catch, and the chain render() -> requestRenderFrame -> handleRenderFrame -> performRender -> renderSheet -> gridCanvas.render (worksheet.ts:5426-5457, 5945, 5985) has no error handling (the only try sites, :688, :3341, :4873, are drag/paste). The new step code clamps only the low side (sheet.ts:4208-4209) and now also evaluates formatValue with the unbounded target inside changeDecimals (sheet.ts:4295). Untrusted-file-driven, persisted to the collaborative document, and reproducible for every collaborator, so it is unsafe handling of attacker-controlled input causing a stored availability failure, not merely a style nit.

finding.summary: `safeFormat`'s fallback re-throws for the same bad argument, so an untrusted `dp`/`cu` in stored style crashes every render (persistent client-side DoS)
finding.evidence: `safeFormat` (format.ts:14-18) catches a failure from `value.toLocaleString(locale, options)` and retries with `'en-US'` and the *same* `options`. The only errors Intl raises here are argument errors — `RangeError: minimumFractionDigits value is out of range` (dp > 20/100) and `RangeError: Invalid currency code` (a `cu` that is not a well-formed ISO code) — and neither is fixed by changing the locale, so the retry throws again and the RangeError escapes `formatValue`. `formatValue` is called unguarded in the render path (`packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1596` with `style?.dp` and `currency: style?.cu`, no try/catch) and now also from the new `Sheet.unsetKeepsRendering` (`sheet.ts:4294-4295`, which passes `currency: effective?.cu` straight from stored cell style). Attack: a crafted .xlsx whose `numFmt` code has >20 decimal placeholders reaches `{ nf: 'number', dp: decimalPlaces(...) }` (`packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-styles.ts:297`) with no upper bound, or a malicious collaborator writes `{nf:'currency', cu:'XX!'}`/`{dp: 300}` into the shared document; every client that renders that cell then throws inside the canvas draw loop and the sheet stops rendering for everyone, persistently, because the bad value is stored. Root cause is pre-existing (the diff relocates the write and adds one new call site), so treat it as a hardening gap this change inherits: `formatValue` should clamp `dp` and validate `cu` (or the fallback should drop the offending option) before handing them to Intl.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is verifiable in the repo. `safeFormat` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/format.ts:14-18) catches the Intl failure and retries with a different locale but the SAME options object, so argument-level RangeErrors (minimum/maximumFractionDigits out of range, invalid currency code) are re-thrown and escape `formatValue`. The `dp` fed into those options is attacker-controlled and unbounded: `decimalPlaces` (xlsx-styles.ts:178-181) returns the raw zero-run length from an arbitrary `formatCode` string with no cap, and is stored into cell style via lines 279/282/297 and 412; a formatCode with >100 zeros after the decimal point yields a `dp` Intl rejects. The consumer is unguarded: `gridcanvas.ts:1596-1598` (and 1777-1779) calls `formatValue(rawData, style?.nf, style?.dp, {currency: style?.cu})` inside `renderCellContent`, and a grep for `try {`/`catch` across gridcanvas.ts returns zero matches, so the throw propagates out of the draw loop invoked at lines 689/749. The new call site is also present as described at sheet.ts:4292-4295, passing `effective?.cu` from stored style. No clamping or validation exists anywhere: `types.ts:100-101` declares `cu?: string`/`dp?: number` unconstrained, and a repo-wide search for fraction-digit clamping finds only the three unguarded uses in format.ts. Impact is a persistent client-side DoS: the bad value is stored, so every render of that cell throws for every client. No refutation ground applies — the code is present as described, no guard renders it unreachable, and untrusted-input handling that breaks a persistent render path is within the Security lens's unsafe-input-handling lane.
